Corollary
[Strictly convex domain] 1. ch6:6.24’\group gt-ch06 If $a^{ij}\in C^\alpha (\Omega )$ and $\Omega $ is bounded and strictly convex, then $a^{ij}D_{ij}u=0$ has a solution in $C^0( ar\Omega )\cap C^{2,\alpha }(\Omega )$ for every continuous boundary datum.

Let $d(x)=\operatorname {dist}(x,\partial \Omega )$ near a $C^2$ boundary point and let $\psi \ge 0$ vanish only at $x_0$. A sufficient local-barrier condition is egin{equation} ag {6.55} K(a^{ij}D_{ij}d+b^iD_i d)\le -k|L\psi |-|f-c\varphi (x_0)| \end{equation} for suitable $K,k>0$. If the principal curvatures with respect to the inner normal are $\kappa _i$ and $a_i$ are the corresponding principal coefficients, egin{equation} ag {6.56} (a^{ij}D_{ij}d)(x_0)=-\sum _{i=1}^{n-1}a_i\kappa _i. \end{equation} Thus the sufficient condition is egin{equation} ag {6.57} \sum _{i=1}^{n-1}a_i\kappa _i>\sup _\Omega |b|, \end{equation} and with continuous $b$ the sharper condition is egin{equation} ag {6.58} \sum _{i=1}^{n-1}a_i\kappa _i-b_ u >0. \end{equation} Let \[ \Sigma _1=\{ x_0:(6.58) ext{ holds}\} ,\qquad \Sigma _2=\{ x_0:a^{ij}v_i v_j e 0 ext{ for a normal }v\} . \]
